subject: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations

messages.author: 9a834fc28d2380a7
messages.subject: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Chris,

I had originally discarded data with error ellipses I felt were too great for the work I was doing, but after having seen your talk at TWS a few weeks ago I am strongly considering trying to include all error into my analyses. Unfortunately, I can't figure out a way to do this in ctmm. I am using the r-package sigloc to triangulate locations, which gives variance in X, variance in Y, a covariance XY and an angle differential (?) as outputs for the estimate variance. 

If you have any advice on what direction I could go to tackle this, it would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Chris,

If you can get point estimates and error ellipses, then that's most of the challenge. The rest is formatting.

At the moment, the easiest way to get sigloc error ellipses into ctmm is probably:
  1. Project the location point estimates from sigloc back to long-lat
  2. Import the long-lat point estimates (with their timestamps) into ctmm as location data, but provide the same projection that was used in sigloc to calculate the error ellipses.
  3. Copy over the sigloc variance/covariance columns into ctmm telemetry object columns COV.x.x,COV.y.y,COV.x.y
I think that should do it. You should be able to plot the location data and see their error ellipses the same as in sigloc.

I've read the paper sigloc is based on (Lenth, 1981) and a newer method (ATM: Gerber et al, 2018). If there is demand, I could probably put something directly into ctmm. It looks like the sigloc package is no longer maintained and I was told that development completed on the ATM package as well.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 9a834fc28d2380a7
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for the feedback. sigloc operates using UTMs - so I am assuming the variance/covariance per location is in meters. In my import file, I had already converted my UTMs to lat/long before importing into ctmm for analysis. Are the variance/covariance columns in ctmm telemetry objects based off long-lat units, or meters, or can they be specified? It would save me a bit of work if I didn't have to run sigloc again (especially considering it is no longer maintained.) 

I wasn't aware of ATM - thanks for that. I will look into it.

I think it would be useful to have a triangulation method for those researchers still using the VHF in ctmm. For many small animals, it is currently the only way to track - and $$$ will keep people using VHF for a while until costs come down for small GPS loggers. Although, with R, as long as packages are compatible with each other it may be redundant to write it in the package if it is already working in another package. 

Thanks again,

Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Chris,

I believe both sigloc and ctmm store the error ellipse information the same way, in square meters, just with different column names. I think you can copy them over directly if you use the same projection. I doubt the UTM projection, specifically, is necessary for sigloc to function, but some locally flat x-y projection is necessary.

Best,
Chris

parts:
Hi Chris,

Thanks for your help earlier. I have a bit of an update on my end. Two things:

1. Copy/pasting my error info from sigloc into the telemetry object as COV.x.x, etc. seemed to work, but I'm not really seeing any difference between home ranges with and without errors. This could be because the errors are so large relative to where the points are located to eachother. I did encounter one error when trying to plot location data (with error = 1):

Error in pracma::ellipke(sqrt(1 - B2)) : 
  Some elements of argument 'm' are out of range.

The result was a blank plot. I think it's because some of my errors are relatively large compared to others (like an order of magnitude or two, from 80m --> 4000m); they are also large on points very close together. When I removed those points from the dataset I no longer encountered the error, and it plotted with error ellipses - however in some cases this did not work.

I've attached code and some sample data. 

2. I'm trying to brainstorm how to get error "ellipses" from the ATM/razimuth package into ctmm. The razimuth output isn't as easy as the copy/paste from sigloc. The advantage for me is that I get associated error with locations that the package sigloc was unable to find a maximum likelihood estimate for, and kind of a likelihood density plot associated with each point instead of just ellipses. 

Is there any chance you've given more thought into incorporating ATM error "ellipses" into ctmm? 

I've also attached some code and sample data which should give an example of razimuth output, if you are interested.

Cheers,

Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Chris,

It looks like you did not turn error on in the model guess before fitting. Error is off by default. See the error vignette: https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/error.html

Some of those COV values have very impossible values, which imply negative variances along one axis. I can fix the plot function to handle small errors, but those are relatively large.

If you have a probability density, then from that you can either calculate the mean location & covariance matrix or you can calculate the mode & local curvature to construct the error ellipses.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Marie,

1. This doesn't look like it will necessarily be in the same projection. You will want to make sure that COV is calculated in the same projection as the data are in (or vice versa). Then, with newer versions of the package, you will want to fix the error information stored in the telemetry object with something like this:

DATA <- as.telemetry(sk.locs)
uere(DATA) <- 1 # you need this in newer versions of the package!

DATA$COV.x.x <- sk.locs$COV.x.x
DATA$COV.y.y <- sk.locs$COV.y.y
DATA$COV.x.y <- sk.locs$COV.x.y

DATA$VAR.xy <- (DATA$COV.x.x + DATA$COV.y.y)/2
plot(DATA)

2. Alternatively, you can use the Argos error-ellipse format ( https://groups.google.com/g/ctmm-user/c/-71Ej-5mOAI/m/xWpBzt0YBAAJ ), although it is annoying to convert from covariance matrices to Argos columns. If COV is a covariance matrix, then the following code should give you the Argos format sqrt(2)-error-ellipse (but please check the outputs):

EIGEN <- eigen(COV)
v <- EIGEN$values
Argos.semi.major <- sqrt(2*v[1])
Argos.semi.minor <- sqrt(2*v[2])
u <- EIGEN$vectors[,1] # major axis eigenvector
theta <- atan2(u[2],u[1]) # angle from x-axis in radians
theta <- theta *360/(2*pi) # angle from x-axis in degrees
Argos.orientation <- theta - 90 # angle from y-axis in degrees

The advantage with this is that you do it before as.telemetry() and then you don't have to worry about the projection.

3.  I haven't coded up uere.fit() for error ellipses yet, because I haven't run into a case where this is necessary. VHF triangulations (and Argos fixes) have a error ellipse specified at a number of standard deviations or quantile. uere.fit() is designed for GPS DOP values where you don't know how many meters of error 1 unit of DOP actually corresponds to.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: f5989a05baac184d
messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Thanks Chris!

This seemed to work concerning your projection comment (aka the error ellipses look correct), but I wanted to run it by you to make sure it's doing what I think it is:

nad83z10 <- "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0"
DATA <- as.telemetry(sk.locs, projection=CRS(nad83z10))

Best,
Marie

messages.subject: Re: Incorporating error ellipses from VHF triangulations
parts:
Hi Marie,

Other than that, if your long-lat aren't in the default datum of WGS84, then you will want to specify that argument as well, like:

datum="+proj=longlat +datum= NAD83"

Otherwise, as.telemetry() will assume the input long-lat are WGS84.

Best,
Chris

On Thursday, November 17, 2022 at 9:53:36 PM UTC-5 tosa....@gmail.com wrote:
Thanks Chris!

This seemed to work concerning your projection comment (aka the error ellipses look correct), but I wanted to run it by you to make sure it's doing what I think it is:

nad83z10 <- "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=NAD83 +units=m +no_defs +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0"
DATA <- as.telemetry(sk.locs, projection=CRS(nad83z10))

Best,
Marie
On Thursday, November 17, 2022 at 3:43:33 PM UTC-8 chris.h...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Marie,

1. This doesn't look like it will necessarily be in the same projection. You will want to make sure that COV is calculated in the same projection as the data are in (or vice versa). Then, with newer versions of the package, you will want to fix the error information stored in the telemetry object with something like this:

DATA <- as.telemetry(sk.locs)
uere(DATA) <- 1 # you need this in newer versions of the package!
DATA$COV.x.x <- sk.locs$COV.x.x
DATA$COV.y.y <- sk.locs$COV.y.y
DATA$COV.x.y <- sk.locs$COV.x.y
DATA$VAR.xy <- (DATA$COV.x.x + DATA$COV.y.y)/2
plot(DATA)

2. Alternatively, you can use the Argos error-ellipse format ( https://groups.google.com/g/ctmm-user/c/-71Ej-5mOAI/m/xWpBzt0YBAAJ ), although it is annoying to convert from covariance matrices to Argos columns. If COV is a covariance matrix, then the following code should give you the Argos format sqrt(2)-error-ellipse (but please check the outputs):

EIGEN <- eigen(COV)
v <- EIGEN$values
Argos.semi.major <- sqrt(2*v[1])
Argos.semi.minor <- sqrt(2*v[2])
u <- EIGEN$vectors[,1] # major axis eigenvector
theta <- atan2(u[2],u[1]) # angle from x-axis in radians
theta <- theta *360/(2*pi) # angle from x-axis in degrees
Argos.orientation <- theta - 90 # angle from y-axis in degrees

The advantage with this is that you do it before as.telemetry() and then you don't have to worry about the projection.

3.  I haven't coded up uere.fit() for error ellipses yet, because I haven't run into a case where this is necessary. VHF triangulations (and Argos fixes) have a error ellipse specified at a number of standard deviations or quantile. uere.fit() is designed for GPS DOP values where you don't know how many meters of error 1 unit of DOP actually corresponds to.

Best,
Chris

On Wednesday, November 16, 2022 at 4:55:46 PM UTC-5 tosa....@gmail.com wrote:

I'm trying to do something similar with VHF triangulations. When I try to plot, it gives me a warning: "DOP values missing. Assuming DOP=1." and when I try uere.fit with and without those columns, I get the same values for both models.
